decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm overhead approach to red; raise clearance while rotating gripper downward. Right arm remains at origin.
Retry from unchanged origin with half-size increments to preserve IK continuity.
Continue smooth elbow-up left approach and downward rotation toward red.
Advance left wrist with clearance, keeping gradual downward pitch and monitoring red in both views.
Move over red with open left fingers, refining lateral alignment and approaching vertical gripper orientation.
Finish vertical orientation and refine red centering from wrist RGB; keep height until jaw alignment is clearer.
Use wrist view to bring red between the open finger pads with a shallow descent.
Fine-align red in the left wrist view and descend a further small amount before closing.
Close left gripper on the centered red block and observe pad contact before lifting.
Lift red vertically with left gripper commanded closed; verify retention visually.
Red did not rise with the fingers. Reopen, shift slightly back, and approach a deeper grasp rather than assuming retention.
Lower open left jaws another 3 cm around red; previous lift showed the first grasp was too shallow.
Descent met resistance; stop lowering. Close at the current depth and make a small visual retention test.
Raise red with closed left gripper; confirm its motion relative to the table before transferring toward orange.
Red is visibly retained. Carry it toward orange with extra vertical clearance, keeping the left arm on its side.
Red slipped during transfer. Stop lateral motion, reopen, and lower above its new visible location to recover it.
Recover red with a straighter, deeper overhead approach and slight backward alignment, leaving jaws open.
Correct fore-aft grasp alignment: red is too low in the wrist view. Shift open jaws back at fixed height, not farther downward.
Close and settle left fingers on red at the corrected fore-aft alignment, without translating during closure.
Lift red straight up after settled closure; watch that it stays seated between the finger pads.
Red stays seated in the jaws. Begin a slower, elevated transfer toward orange, maintaining the closed grip.
Continue slow transfer of retained red toward the orange base, keeping clearance and left-side configuration.
Bring red above the orange base using head and wrist alignment; stay just left of center with the gripper closed.
Replan after the two-step prefix: smaller inward increments and a controlled descent to improve reach margin while approaching orange.
Fine-align red over orange with small inward/forward increments and shallow descent, monitoring the reach limit.
Near the reach boundary, use a small inward gripper tilt instead of extending the arm farther; keep red held and descend only slightly.
Make millimeter-scale final alignment over orange and lower red toward contact, retaining the small inward tilt for reach margin.
Set red down gently on the orange base and open the left gripper while holding the placement pose.
Withdraw the open left gripper to inspect the red-on-orange placement; begin gradual right-arm approach to yellow.
Red appears stable on orange. Retreat left toward its origin while advancing the right arm smoothly toward yellow.
Retry the unchanged pose with smaller left retreat increments to satisfy joint continuity; continue the right approach only if accepted.
Red has toppled beside orange. Return the open left gripper to recover it, correcting its tilt; continue right approach to yellow separately.
Align open left jaws with the fallen red, and continue right wrist toward a vertical yellow pickup with separate workspaces.
Refine left red alignment and begin closure without further pressing. Finish the right vertical approach to yellow.
Settle the red grasp and test a small vertical lift. Fine-align yellow and close the right gripper without lateral motion during closure.
Lift recovered red above orange with modest inward tilt for reach, while settling and gently lifting yellow to verify its grasp.
Shift held red farther over orange, including forward correction missing from the prior placement; lift retained yellow safely and keep arms separate.
Release red at the improved centered placement without further downward pressure; keep yellow stationary and held.
Red appears seated on orange. Clear the open left gripper gently and begin slow yellow transfer with right-arm clearance.
Continue withdrawing left without touching the stable red-orange stack; carry yellow slowly inward at clearance height.
Increase left gripper clearance without further rotation and inspect stack stability. Move retained yellow toward staging with a small inward tilt.
The stack has separated. Pause yellow safely; approach orange with left to bring the base closer for a more reachable, stable stack.
Approach orange with the open left jaws, using the forward-tilted pose to keep elbow-up reach margin. Yellow remains held still.
Complete orange alignment and shallow descent, then begin left closure to relocate the base.
Settle orange closure, then test a small vertical lift before relocating the base. Keep yellow still and closed.
Orange is held between the pads. Move its base location closer to the robot and toward center, without crossing the left arm.
Carry orange to a central, closer table location that both arms can reach with elbow-up margin; keep orientation fixed.
Lower orange toward the table at the new central base location, holding its orientation steady before release.
Open left fingers to leave orange on the table; wait for release before a strictly vertical clearance move.
Raise open left gripper straight up with fixed orientation to clear the relocated orange base without disturbing it.
Orange is clear on the table at the closer location. Move the open left gripper above red for a new pickup while yellow stays held.
Advance the left gripper over red with a gradual descent, keeping the successful forward-tilted pickup orientation.
Fine-align red between left pads at the same pickup height used for orange, keeping yellow stationary.
Make a small lateral red correction, close left fingers, and let the grasp settle before lifting.
Finish closing on red, then lift vertically to verify retention before transferring to the relocated orange.
Red is visibly retained. Transfer toward the closer orange base with a clearance lift and fixed wrist orientation.
Carry red above the relocated orange using the same fixed tilt and approximate base pickup offset; maintain height until centered.
Fine-align red over orange with a small rightward/backward correction and gentle descent; preserve fixed orientation for release.
Release red over the centered orange base and wait with the wrist fixed; next retreat will be strictly vertical to avoid disturbing the stack.
Lift the open left gripper vertically with fixed orientation to inspect whether red is supported; yellow remains stationary.
Red remains supported after vertical clearance. Move left safely aside while bringing retained yellow above the closer stack.
Withdraw left toward origin after clearing the stack. Align right-held yellow over red with slow inward/backward motion at clearance height.
Use head alignment to center yellow over red and lower carefully. Continue left-arm return through a smooth elbow-up path.
Make a millimeter-scale yellow centering correction without further descent; continue the left arm toward its recorded origin.
Open right fingers to leave yellow on red, keeping its wrist fixed for settling. Finish the smooth left-arm return near origin.
Clear yellow with a strictly vertical right-gripper lift, keeping its orientation unchanged. Correct the last small left-origin residual.
All three blocks remain stacked after clearance. Withdraw right outward and backward, beginning a continuous elbow-up return to origin.
Retry the unchanged right pose with half-sized retreat and rotation increments after the continuity rejection.
Continue gradual right-arm return away from the stable stack, lowering only after horizontal clearance.
Return the open right arm toward origin through a smooth elbow-up path; the three-block stack remains undisturbed.
Continue the right-arm reset with gradual translation and orientation recovery; left stays at origin and both grippers remain open.
Bring the right arm closer to its recorded origin while preserving configuration continuity and leaving the stack untouched.
